title: Coloratura and spatial-audio navigation
dek: A game designed to be navigable without sight will eventually be tested by the players its design claims to serve.
whyTracked: The project makes specific, consequential accessibility claims whose real test arrives with a playable build and independent evaluation by blind players.

current.assessment: The design intentions are unusually concrete, but the public evidence remains first-party and pre-release. Practical accessibility is not yet established.
current.nextReviewTrigger: Review on a demo, release-date announcement, public launch, independent blind-player evaluation, or material accessibility patch.

openQuestions: How will blind players evaluate navigation and comfort in the released game?
How dependent is the experience on headphones, spatial-audio hardware, or particular hearing profiles?
Will post-release feedback produce design changes?

watchFor.description: A release date or playable public build
watchFor.trigger: The developer announces a date, demo, beta, or launch.
Blind reviewers and accessibility specialists document the finished experience.
Patches or developer notes respond to player accessibility findings.

observations.headline: Point-zero observation
observations.summary: Nakama Game Studio described Coloratura as a free-moving 3D PlayStation 5 adventure designed to be navigable without sight through positional sound, objective audio, broad geometry, and blind playtesting.

sources.title: Coloratura: designing a world where sound is the only guide

observations.headline: Admitted to The Wake pilot
observations.summary: Admitted because the advertised accessibility design has a clearly identifiable future test and should not be judged only by promotional intent.
